clue.text: Ageing old boy's unique smell

parts.note: an old boy is a former pupil, abbreviated OB; the 's is a link meaning has
sole means one and only, unique
a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: An elderly former pupil gives off a peculiar odour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something becoming outdated is in the process of growing old, or going out of use.

clue.text: Robber's outfit hidden in crowd

definitions.note: read as Robber is: the 's is the link joining definition and wordplay

indicators.note: something hidden in a crowd sits inside it, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: a band is a group or crowd of people
a rig is an outfit of clothes

explanation.surface: A thief's disguise is concealed among a throng of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden in' suggests a hidden word, but here it puts RIG inside BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit or highway thief is a robber.

clue.text: Running exercise class on oxygen

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
PE is physical education, school exercise
a rating is a class or grade

explanation.surface: A gym session is held for a group, with breathing apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the pieces after O, which sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is working or functioning is running.

clue.text: Group of men on the pull!

definitions.text: Group of men on the pull!

parts.words: Group of men on the pull!
parts.note: a pack of men out looking for romance, but really a rowing crew of that many hauling on their oars

explanation.surface: A gang of lads out on the town trying to pick people up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing crew of that size heaves on the oars, so pulls together.

clue.text: Hurt end of jaw catching a good right

indicators.note: catching means holding the other letters inside

parts.note: the chin is the front end of the jaw

explanation.surface: A boxer feels the pain when a fine right hook lands on the chin.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurt as a noun is wounded feelings, mortification or vexation.

clue.text: Roman god of song on new record

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a tune is a song

explanation.surface: A Roman deity's anthem appears on a fresh release.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue TUNE 'on' N plus EP sits below them.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the Roman deity of the sea, counterpart of the Greek Poseidon.

clue.text: Bogus cure — often it's hopeless

indicators.note: hopeless means made a mess of, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: read as it is: IT is the fodder and 's the link

explanation.surface: A quack remedy usually fails to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Fake or forged things are bogus.

clue.text: A female's weak but fiery

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female; the 's is a link meaning is
a lame excuse is a weak one

explanation.surface: A woman is feeble yet hot-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on fire, or glowing with passion, is fiery.

clue.text: Sour face — in no position to score!

parts.note: milk that has gone sour is off
a side is a face, as of a cube

explanation.surface: A grumpy look from a footballer who cannot put the ball in the net.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a player in front of the last defender when the ball is played cannot legally score.
explanation.definitionFit: A football player caught beyond the defence is penalised, so in no legal position for a goal.

clue.text: Takes advantage of opening of government files

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: rasps are coarse files, and to rasp is to file

explanation.surface: Ministers exploit a leak from Whitehall's records.
explanation.definitionFit: Seizing an opportunity is grabbing it, so exploiting it.

clue.text: On the touchline, but she's no reserve!

definitions.text: On the touchline, but she's no reserve!

parts.words: On the touchline, but she's no reserve!
parts.note: sounds like a substitute waiting to play, but reserve means restraint: she is beside the pitch whipping up the crowd, anything but restrained

explanation.surface: A woman waits beside the pitch but is not a substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: A pom-pom waving performer stands by the field and is famously unrestrained.

clue.text: Falls back once more holding case of retsina…

indicators.note: back means the word is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: again means once more

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer pair of letters

explanation.surface: Someone relapses into drinking more Greek wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is loose here: RA, the first and last letters of 'retsina', follows NIAGA (AGAIN turned by 'back') rather than going inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border bear this name.

clue.text: …due to finding his head in ditch

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: a trough is a channel or ditch

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone ends up head first in a gutter after the drinking of the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening because of a cause happens by way of it, owing to it.

clue.text: Rewrite pieces penned by journalist

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: ED is an editor, a journalist
chessmen are pieces, so men

explanation.surface: A reporter writes articles that need revising.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct a text is to revise or rewrite it.

clue.text: Unfaithful siren with nice shape

indicators.note: to shape something is to form it anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seductress with a fine figure proves untrue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone false or two-faced is not faithful to their word.

clue.text: Feeling full, as if diet's working

indicators.note: working means being worked on, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: the 's here supplies a letter S to the fodder

explanation.surface: A slimmer feels sated as though the eating plan is succeeding.
explanation.definitionFit: After a good meal one is replete and content.

clue.text: Caution — dubious gift horse!

indicators.note: dubious means doubtful or suspect, so these letters are not to be trusted as they stand

explanation.surface: Wariness about a suspect present, echoing never look a gift horse in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudent planning ahead for what may go wrong is a kind of caution.

clue.text: Dashing a long way round on search

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the word reads the other way

parts.note: far means a long way
to fish is to search or grope around

explanation.surface: A dashing figure travels far and wide hunting for something.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue FISH 'on' RAF sits beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rakish, jaunty and slightly disreputable people are dashing.

clue.text: It helps to move higher round horse's middle

indicators.note: round means placed around the other letters

parts.note: to stir is to move
up means higher

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word horse

explanation.surface: Something aids a rider in climbing up on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: A rider puts a foot in this loop to mount, so the whole clue paints it too.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider's foot rest is a help, an aid in getting into the saddle.

clue.text: Curious animal moans extremely loudly, initially

definitions.text: Curious animal moans extremely loudly, initially

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: An odd beast groans at great volume.
explanation.definitionFit: The ship of the desert is a curious beast known for its loud groaning.

clue.text: Part of church opening on left? Not usually

parts.note: a chance is an opening or opportunity

explanation.surface: Someone queries which side of a church a doorway is on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not usually' is a wry comment: the east end of a church is not usually on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: The east end of a church round the altar, used by clergy and choir.

clue.text: Misses second run out by seconds

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A cricketer laments a second batter run out by a fraction of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Grieving for someone gone means sorely missing them.

clue.text: Lay one on national front — soundly trounced

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
NF is the abbreviation for the National Front party

indicators.note: soundly signals that a word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: licked means thoroughly beaten, trounced

explanation.surface: Someone lands a blow on a far-right party which is roundly beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Front is a British far-right party, NF.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay a tax or punishment on someone is to impose it.

clue.text: Sharp tongue on Tory leader

indicators.note: a leader is the first letter of the word

parts.note: Erse is the Gaelic tongue of Ireland or Scotland

explanation.surface: A Conservative chief has a cutting manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Curt, brusque speech is sharp.

clue.text: Doctor's aid for depression?

parts.note: suggests a treatment for low mood, but the depression is physical: pressing down a patient's tongue to look at the throat

explanation.surface: A medic seeks a remedy for low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat blade, used by a doctor as a tongue depressor.

clue.text: Newspaper copy…

definitions.meaning: a British tabloid daily of that name
to reflect or imitate something exactly

explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A British tabloid paper shares its name with a looking glass, and to reflect is to imitate.

clue.text: …for hack off independent with new intelligence, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: sense means intelligence, good judgement

explanation.surface: A reporter leaves an independent paper with fresh news.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 25: 'hack off' is the definition, British slang for annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrage someone is to annoy them, or hack them off.

clue.text: Proprietary furniture stripper?

definitions.meaning: furniture made by and named after an eighteenth-century English cabinet maker
a member of a male striptease troupe of that name

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Chippendale's chairs bear his name, as does a famous male revue troupe.
